english.title: Act of violence at a civil airport likely to cause death / personal injury and endanger safe operation
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[a device,]_
(B)_[devices,]_
(C)_[a substance,]_
(D)_[substances,]_
(E)_[a weapon,]_
(F)_[weapons,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE DEVICE, SUBSTANCE OR WEAPON..), at an aerodrome serving international civil aviation, namely **(..SPECIFY..), intentionally committed an act of violence which was likely to cause death or serious personal injury

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See subsection 1(3) for extra-territorial jurisdiction.
(ii) See subsection 1(9) for definitions.
(iii) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution.
(iv) See also associated offence wordings as follows: H4454 and H4455.
(v) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
Life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
